sections.label: Prime Minister appoints EBRC
sections.summary: The Prime Minister appoints the EBRC, sets its terms, and need not reveal when it is formed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Prime Minister appoints an Electoral Boundaries Review Committee (EBRC) and sets its terms of reference.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Once the EBRC publishes its report with the new electoral boundaries, Parliament is dissolved and a General Election (GE) held shortly after.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, the Prime Minister does not have to reveal when the EBRC will be formed or whether he has formed the EBRC.

sections.label: EBRC voter deviation allowance
sections.summary: Since 1980 the EBRC has allowed average voters per MP to deviate by plus or minus 30%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Since 1980, the EBRC has also allowed the average number of voters per MP to deviate by plus or minus 30%, up from 20% previously.

sections.label: Fixing voter numbers in law
sections.summary: The average number of voters per MP and allowable deviations should be fixed into law.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The average number of voters per MP and the allowable deviations should be fixed into law.

sections.label: PSP proposes 30,000 voters per MP
sections.summary: PSP proposes one MP represent 30,000 voters, with plus or minus 10% deviation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: PSP proposes that one MP should represent 30,000 voters, with a deviation of plus or minus 10%, such that each MP represents 27,000 to 33,000 voters.

sections.label: Minimum timeframe before General Election
sections.summary: PSP proposes a minimum three months between the EBRC report and dissolution of Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Three, ensure political fairness by imposing a minimum timeframe from finalising boundaries to GE.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We propose a minimum period of three months between the publishing of EBRC report to the dissolution of Parliament.

sections.label: Prime Minister controls boundary review
sections.summary: The Prime Minister has full control over the electoral boundary review process.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In our system, the Prime Minister has full control over the electoral boundary review process.

sections.label: EBRC chair and members
sections.summary: PSP proposes the EBRC be chaired by a High Court Judge with four other members from ELD, HDB, SLA and the Chief Statistician.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: PSP proposes that EBRC be chaired by a High Court Judge with four other members being the CEOs of ELD, HDB and SLA, and the Chief Statistician.

sections.label: MP voter representation range
sections.summary: PSP proposes legislation that each MP represent only between 27,000 and 33,000 voters to reduce disparity and unfairness.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The PSP proposes legislation to stipulate that each MP can only represent between 27,000 and 33,000 voters to reduce the current significant disparity and unfairness to voters and MPs.

sections.label: EBRC report release timing
sections.summary: The EBRC report should be released at least three months before Parliament's dissolution so parties can prepare for the GE.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Fourthly, the release of the EBRC report should be at least three months before the dissolution of Parliament to allow all political parties sufficient time to prepare for the GE.

sections.label: EBRC reporting and PSP proposals
sections.summary: The EBRC should report directly to Parliament, which should immediately approve and implement it without modifications, and PSP's proposal lists transparency, fairness, anti-gerrymandering, timing and independence measures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: To avoid suspicion, the EBRC should not report to the Prime Minister but should submit the report directly to Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Upon receiving the report, Parliament should immediately approve and implement it without any modifications to ensure fairness and transparency of the process. : In summary, PSP's proposal seeks to: (a) increase transparency and accountability by: one, requiring the formation of EBRC to be publicly announced immediately; two, requiring EBRC to, upon its formation, publish the current number of voters in each constituency based on boundaries in the last GE; and three, requiring EBRC to publicly and sufficiently explain all changes; (b) ensure fairness to voters by narrowing the range of number of voters per MP; (c) respect voters and reduce the potential for gerrymandering by: one, implementing fixed rules through major and minor boundaries; and two, requiring changes of major boundaries to be approved by a bipartisan committee; (d) increase political fairness by imposing a minimum timeframe from finalising boundaries to GE; and (e) enhance the independence of EBRC.

sections.label: Grid subdivision counting examples
sections.summary: A four-by-four grid offers 117 subdivisions into four contiguous four-square districts, a six-by-six grid over 451,000 options, and a nine-by-nine grid seven hundred trillion.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Even a simple four-by-four grid, an unrealistically simple map if there ever was one, offers up 117 ways to subdivide these 16 squares, such that there are four districts with four contiguous squares in each.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: A six-by-six grid will present more than 451,000 options and there are seven hundred trillion ones in a nine-by-nine grid.

sections.label: Seat-vote margin electoral advantage
sections.summary: Calculations for GE2020 show an electoral advantage of about 17% from districting alone, below the gap between PAP's 61% vote share and 89% seat share.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: It boils down, actually, to a simple equation which tallies the difference between seat and vote margins.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: I did the calculations and, for GE2020, this amounted to an electoral advantage of about 17%, owing not to credible aspects of the different parties but simply to the system of districting alone, at least according to this interpretation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: This, significantly, notably, is below the gap one saw between the People's Action Party's (PAP's) share of the popular vote of 61% versus its seat share of 89%, but it nevertheless offers some sense of how much PAP might currently benefit from the way that electoral boundaries are currently drawn.

sections.label: Redistricting algorithms and human oversight
sections.summary: A 2017 Singapore workshop trained participants in redistricting techniques, and the speaker favours human oversight but supports publishing deviations from algorithmic districts.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Indeed, in 2017, Singaporeans even participated in a workshop meant to train participants on applying these techniques, although I do not know if the individual or individuals attending were members of EBRC.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Even if we remain uncomfortable with completely delegating the redistricting task to automation, I personally would still favour human hands at the tiller.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: But in my view, publishing any adjustments and deviations from districts proposed by such algorithms would nevertheless constitute an important step forward in fairness.

sections.label: Benchmarking electoral bounds
sections.summary: Benchmarking existing electoral bounds against mathematically vetted ones would improve transparency and make maps more acceptable.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Benchmarking our existing electoral bounds against these that have passed mathematical muster would improve transparency and make these maps more acceptable to everyone involved.

sections.label: Support for the Motion
sections.summary: The speaker states that for these reasons he supports the Motion.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: For these reasons, Mr Speaker, I support the Motion.

sections.label: Close races and GRC incorporation
sections.summary: Low Thia Khiang's 1996 table showed SMCs with close races were incorporated into GRCs, citing Braddell Heights 1991 and Joo Chiat 2011.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As far back as 1996, then-MP for Hougang, Mr Low Thia Khiang, presented a table in this House that showed how SMCs that had been through close electoral races were invariably incorporated into GRCs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 1991, the opposition candidate in Braddell Heights, Mr Sin Kek Tong, obtained close to 48% of the vote.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 2011, the Workers' Party's (WP's) Yee Jenn Jong obtained close to 49% of the vote, losing the SMC of Joo Chiat by a mere 388 votes.

sections.label: Lee Kuan Yew's opposition speeches
sections.summary: Quotes about placing delineation reasons before an all-party Committee came from Lee Kuan Yew's 1956 and 1957 opposition speeches.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Nothing would be lost, if the reasons for the delineations are placed before an all-party Committee".

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It should not surprise this House to learn that these quotes were from Parliamentary speeches made by Mr Lee Kuan Yew in 1956 and 1957 when he was in the opposition.

sections.label: Boundary review timing rules
sections.summary: Boundary delineation occurs every eight years, not before a general election, and Canada bars using revised boundaries within seven months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In addition, the boundary delineation exercise takes place once every eight years, and not before a general election.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In Canada, there is an additional stipulation that revised boundaries cannot be used for elections within seven months of the revision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Any election within that period would run using the previous boundaries.

sections.label: WP proposes electoral boundary system
sections.summary: The WP asks the Government to consider legislating a system with five listed features.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The WP asks the Government to consider legislating and implementing a system that includes the following features: first, a Commission that is truly independent whose decisions cannot be rejected by the party in power; second for a Supreme Court Judge selected by the Chief Justice to be appointed as a member of the EBRC; third, the publication of proposed changes well in advance of elections and outside the election cycle; fourth, the opportunity for the public, including political parties, to provide feedback on the proposed changes; and fifth, a minimum period during which revised boundaries cannot be used for elections.

sections.label: Purpose of drawing electoral boundaries
sections.summary: Electoral boundaries are drawn so that the electorate is best served by their MPs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Electoral boundaries are drawn so that the electorate is best served by their MPs.

sections.label: Prime Minister has not convened EBRC
sections.summary: The Prime Minister has not convened the EBRC.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: To answer Ms Poa's question, the Prime Minister has not convened the EBRC.

sections.label: EBRC lacks voting information
sections.summary: The EBRC does not have access to voting information and does not base recommendations on voting patterns.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: First, the EBRC does not have access to voting information and hence, does not make its recommendations based on voting patterns.

sections.label: Judge chairing EBRC rejected
sections.summary: The Government does not think a High Court Judge chairing the EBRC will resolve concerns about political interference.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Ms Hazel Poa suggested that the EBRC be chaired by a High Court Judge – and so did Mr Pritam Singh and Assoc Prof Jamus Lim – to enhance the independence of the EBRC.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: We have thought about this carefully and we have looked at the experiences of other countries, and we do not think that this will resolve the concern about political interference.

sections.label: Electors change residential addresses annually
sections.summary: Some 200,000 electors change their residential addresses annually.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Some 200,000 electors change their residential addresses annually.

sections.label: Electors and electoral roll size
sections.summary: There are 200,000 electors every year and the electoral roll is about 2.7 million.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Maybe I should put this in context: 200,000 electors every year and our electoral roll is about 2.7 million.

sections.label: Planning norm for electors per MP
sections.summary: Since 1980 the planning norm is plus or minus 30% variation in average electors per MP, and lowering it would likely require more disruptive redrawing of boundaries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Since 1980, we have a planning norm of plus or minus 30% variation in the average number of electors per MP.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: In our context, because population shifts between general elections can be quite significant, as I have illustrated, lowering the planning norm would likely require more extensive and more disruptive redrawing of boundaries.

sections.label: Pew survey on democracy satisfaction
sections.summary: A Spring 2024 Pew survey found over three-quarters of interviewed Singaporeans satisfied with democracy, ranking Singapore first in Asia Pacific.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: According to the Spring 2024 Global Attitudes Survey by the Pew Research Center, more than three-quarters of the Singaporeans interviewed were satisfied with the way democracy is working in Singapore and Singapore ranked first within the Asia Pacific region in terms of level of satisfaction with our practice of democracy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: As the survey findings show, we have a trusted electoral system that allows the electorate to vote freely for MPs who do their best in looking after their constituent's interests, representing them in Parliament and forming a government to run the country responsively and responsibly.

sections.label: Trust levels and Motion effect
sections.summary: Trust levels in Singapore are high, but the Motion sows distrust and disaffection.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Trust levels in Singapore, including in Government, are high and even the opposition and many opposition voters will concede that the PAP governments have served Singaporeans well and to the best of our ability.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: However, intentionally or unintentionally, this Motion sows distrust and disaffection.

sections.label: Government opposition to Motion
sections.summary: The Government will oppose the Motion given its false premises about the electoral boundary review process and public officers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The Government will oppose the Motion given its false premises and suggestions that the electoral boundary review process, and our public officers who serve on it, have not been transparent or fair.

sections.label: Increase in EBRC guidelines
sections.summary: The EBRC guidelines have been increased over the years from 20% to 30%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Instead, our EBRC guidelines have been increased over the years – from 20% to 30%.

sections.label: Boundary changes from recommendations
sections.summary: Adopting the recommended suggestions would lead to even more drastic boundary changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: My second point, as I have explained very carefully to Ms Hazel Poa's suggestions, if we adopt and do exactly what you all have recommended, we should expect even more and more drastic boundary changes.

sections.label: Natural movements and gerrymandering risk
sections.summary: Natural movements of 200,000 electors might unintentionally produce a gerrymandered outcome, so benchmark maps were suggested.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Even if we accept this position, it does not exclude the very real possibility that natural movements in the electorate – 200,000 in fact, as Minister Chan just shared – might inadvertently give rise to an unintentional gerrymandered outcome.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: That is why I suggested introducing scientifically supported tools to produce benchmark maps as reference.

sections.label: EBRC lacks polling data
sections.summary: The EBRC has no access to polling results or voting patterns, and the goal is divisions that are microcosms of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: So, I will not go into whether it is intentional, unintentional because I cannot understand your definition of and distinction between those.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We do not give the EBRC and the EBRC has no access to the polling results.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We have no idea what the polling results or the voting pattern of the 200,000 people who have moved; neither do we have data on how the new electors in every election cycle will vote.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Our goal is to make sure that every division is roughly a microcosm of Singapore so that when an election is conducted, people consider the national interest so that we do not have sectoral interests that define a particular division like other countries.

sections.label: Lee Kuan Yew on delineation committee
sections.summary: Lee Kuan Yew said population shifts to new towns meant his office would appoint an Electoral Boundaries Delineation Committee of civil servants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Mr Lee Kuan Yew replied as follows: "As there have been population shifts away from the old centres of populations into the new towns, my office will appoint an Electoral Boundaries Delineation Committee consisting of civil servants.

sections.label: Civil servants keep boundary process
sections.summary: The process is kept as it is so politically unaffiliated civil servants, not political parties, take charge of drawing boundaries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: First, I think I have explained very clearly in my speech why we have kept the process as it is now, so that the civil servants who are not politically affiliated take charge of this process rather than have political parties getting involved and ending up, like in other countries, where there is horse-trading on how the boundaries are to be drawn.

sections.label: Public officers and boundary outcomes
sections.summary: Public officers should not be made responsible for whether a certain party wins or loses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: If the outcome that we are desiring is a set of boundaries that the public servants who have done their work professionally and objectively come up with to the best of their ability, then, that is the outcome.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: If the outcome is about whether a certain party wins or loses, then I am sorry to say that my public officers should not be made responsible for such an outcome.

sections.label: Political system success mark
sections.summary: The mark of success for any political system is not what rules it has.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The mark of success for any political system is not what rules it has.

sections.label: Swing voters survey increase
sections.summary: A survey found swing voters rose from 37.8% in 2015 to 59.2% in 2020, defined as voters with mixed conservative and pluralist views.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In that survey, Sir, it was found that the number of swing voters had increased tremendously from 37.8% in 2015 to 59.2% in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Swing voters were defined as voters who gave an eclectic mix of views of having somewhat conservative views and somewhat pluralist views.

sections.label: Conservative voters decline
sections.summary: Conservative voters, who disagreed on need for change in electoral system, checks and balances, and different voices, fell from 44.3% in 2015 to 18.5% in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The conservative voters were those who disagreed that there is a need for change in the electoral system, checks and balances, and different voices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They went down from 44.3% in 2015 to only 18.5% in 2020.

sections.label: Overt gerrymandering voter reaction
sections.summary: If there was overt gerrymandering, Singaporeans would see it and react accordingly at the ballot.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Because if it was overtly political, if there was overt gerrymandering, Singaporeans would see it and they would react accordingly at the ballot.

sections.label: EBRC recommendations basis
sections.summary: The Minister said the EBRC does not base its recommendations or boundary changes on election results.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: The Minister has said that the EBRC does not make its recommendations or boundary changes based on election results.

sections.label: Boundary changes housing units
sections.summary: Boundary changes depend more on housing units within a boundary than people shifting house yearly, with a plus or minus 10% range deemed doable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: It is more dependent on the number of housing units within a particular boundary, rather than how many people are shifting house each year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: We believe that this range of plus or minus 10%, as it has been implemented in other countries, should be doable and will not result in too frequent changes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: The Minister declared that our current system is fair and transparent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: But he has not given any explanation to explain why is it that the statistics that we have mentioned, about the SMCs where the opposition did better, have a higher chance of disappearing.

sections.label: England constituency boundary review report
sections.summary: The most recent England parliamentary constituency boundary review report explained how constituencies were derived and how geographic features were used as boundaries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: If we look overseas, the most recent report for the review of parliamentary constituency boundaries in England went into detail explaining the reasoning behind how constituencies were derived and how certain geographic features, such as the River Thames or expressways, were used as boundaries.

sections.label: Motion for fairness and accountability
sections.summary: The Motion argues for fairness, transparency and accountability, saying fair political competition gives Singapore a healthier democracy in the national interest.

sentences.text: What we are arguing for in this Motion is for fairness, transparency and accountability.
It is very important to assure that there is fair competition in the political arena because this can only give Singapore a healthier democracy and that is definitely in the national interest.

sections.label: Renewing values under new PM
sections.summary: With a new Prime Minister appointed, the speaker urges renewing the push for important values, saying fairness in GE starts with the boundary review process.

sentences.text: As Singapore enters a new chapter with the appointment of a new Prime Minister, let us renew our push for values that are important to us.
And fairness in GE starts with the boundary review process.

sections.label: Voting results declared
sections.summary: The voting results are declared: 10 Ayes, 76 Noes, and no Abstentions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I will proceed to declare the voting results now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: There are 10 "Ayes", "76 Noes", no "Abstentions".
